newsitem.title: USA: Wake begins for Chicago's Cardinal Bernardin.
newsitem.headline: Wake begins for Chicago's Cardinal Bernardin.

text.p: The body of Cardinal Joseph Bernardin was carried into his cathedral on Monday for a wake that will last around the clock until burial on Wednesday.

In a procession led by motorcycle policemen and followed by five mounted patrolmen, the body of the 68-year-old prelate was driven from his residence several blocks away to Holy Name Cathedral where fire and police officers lining the steps rendered a white-gloved salute.

Children rang handbells, constuction workers removed their hard hats and office workers left their desks to line the funeral procession's route. Bernardin, senior figure in the Roman Catholic Church's U.S. hierarchy and leader of Chicago's 2.3 million-member archdiocese for the past 14 years, died last week of pancreatic cancer.

His body was placed at the steps of the altar next to a flickering paschal candle in the Romanesque limestone cathedral just north of downtown Chicago. Family, including two nephews who acted as pallbearers, close friends and church employees participated in a service of prayer and song.

Among those attending were relatives from his father's birthplace in northern Italy. Afterwards the 1,200 in the church filed past the open casket on two sides, some pausing to touch the white vestments clothing Bernardin's body.
The doors of the cathedral were to remain open day and night for public visitation until Wednesday morning before a funeral mass at noon local time (1800 GMT).

The South-Carolina-born Bernardin was one of the most respected figures in the U.S. Catholic Church, a moderate peacemaker among liberals and conservatives. He had made his battle against terminal cancer a highly visible and spiritual one, saying he welcomed death as a friend, not a conqueror.
The longest-serving active U.S. cardinal, he was appointed by Pope John Paul II in 1982 to head the Chicago archdiocese, the nation's second-largest after Los Angeles.
His body will be entombed in a mausoleum alongside those of other Chicago bishops and cardinals at Mount Carmel Cemetery near Chicago.
